acceptance_matrix.requirement: FF-DEC-002 records and mechanically enforces the exact Operator-approved shipped dependency boundary: future fforager-net may directly use reqwest 0.13.4 and rustls 0.23.42 with rustls-no-provider and native ring 0.17.14; AWS-LC, native-tls, OpenSSL, default-feature, version, consumer, runtime-class, native-link, build-download, prebuilt-binary, and undeclared feature drift are rejected.

Canonical validation distinguishes product-authorized native exceptions from non-shipped-only exceptions, preserves FF-DEC-001's product prohibition, requires exact per-edge attribution, and rejects attempts to route wreq or its native graph into any shipped member.

The non-shipped ordinary candidate resolves and exercises the exact reqwest/rustls/ring graph with system proxies, automatic redirects, cookie storage, automatic decompression, and dependency retry authority disabled; it records that global/per-origin admission and security partitioning remain Ferric-owned.

Requests requiring TLS or HTTP/2 browser fingerprints return a stable typed browser-transport-required refusal before network execution; ordinary transport never silently invokes wreq, weakens requested capabilities, or reports fingerprint compatibility.

The technical design and no-context model manual state the two-engine decision, exact dependency controls, wreq disabled/non-shipped status, known ceilings, future fforager-net consumer, and required FF-GATE-RUNTIME-001 re-proof without claiming product progress.

High-risk distinct-lens subagent review records diff attack surfaces, at least two independent checks, counterfactuals, boundary probes, negative paths, findings, remediations, and residual uncertainty across transport security, resource/lifecycle, and dependency/proof-integrity lenses; every confirmed finding becomes a public-boundary regression and the complete matrix reruns.

The strict final verdict is PASS_ORDINARY_TRANSPORT_DECISION only when every dependency, policy, typed-gap, review, and canonical-gate requirement passes; the verdict retains the prerequisite zero-progress ceiling and cannot be interpreted as shipped downloader behavior.
